title: A proved ordinary quotient adjunction tower with abstract fields
statement: For X, A, J and U and the functors F_n and fixed balancing theta_n of [def-sfb-adic-perfect-module-functors], define SectionModel to consist of right adjoints R_n, adjunctions F_n left adjoint R_n, natural successor maps kappa_n:R_(n+1) to C_n R_n, and the identity eta_n(M)=eta_(n+1)(M) followed by kappa_n(F_(n+1)M) and R_n(theta_n(M)). Construct a SectionModel using the concrete terminal sections adjoints of [def-sfb-adic-perfect-quotient-section-realization] and the unit/counit mates of inverse balancing from [def-sfb-adic-perfect-slice-sections]. Select sectionModel from this completely proved Nonempty theorem and expose its R, a and kappa fields as rightAdjoint, adjunction and step. The selected right adjoints are canonically isomorphic, by adjunction uniqueness, to the concrete sections functors. The selected successor maps satisfy the stored unit identity and hence are the mates of inverse fixed balancing. No unproved theorem is used to choose this data.

proof.text: Use the concrete quotient sections adjunction rawAdjunction, constructed by completion cancellation and transport from the tensor and constant-presheaf adjunctions.

Construct SectionModel.ofAdjunctions for arbitrary R_n and adjunctions a_n:F_n left adjoint R_n. Its successor field is balancingMate(a_n,a_(n+1),theta_n), and balancingMate_unit supplies its unit_eq field. The functors and adjunctions remain parameters throughout this proof; no concrete scalar implementation is unfolded.

Apply SectionModel.ofAdjunctions to rawRightAdjoint and rawAdjunction. This completely proves sectionModel_exists. Select sectionModel from that proved theorem and expose its fields; step_unit is the unit_eq field. The structure interface prevents consumers from normalizing the scalar-extension implementations. The right adjoints of any two models are related by their unique right-adjoint isomorphisms; the unit identity determines each successor map by naturality at the upper counit and the right triangle identity.
